prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “ChatGPT checker” — the best practical approach is to (1) make sure your business is authoritative in the major local knowledge sources (Google Business Profile, Yelp, Foursquare, Apple Maps, Bing) and (2) use a local‑listing management + monitoring service (Yext is the most powerful for feeding many AI/knowledge networks; BrightLocal, Moz Local or Whitespark are good for monitoring). Then spot‑check AI assistants (ChatGPT/Bard/Bing Chat with browsing enabled) with targeted prompts.

Why: generative AIs don’t consult a single directory — they synthesize from knowledge graphs and public listings. So the best way to be “recommended” is to be a high‑quality, consistent source in the data networks those models draw on. The best way to check is a mix of listing monitoring and direct testing.

Recommended services and steps
1. Claim and optimize Google Business Profile (most important). AI models often surface Google Knowledge Panel data for local businesses.
2. Use a knowledge-management service to push authoritative data everywhere:
   - Yext (best single commercial solution to distribute/maintain consistent business data across many providers and feeds used by search/AI).
   - Alternatives: Moz Local, BrightLocal, Synup.
3. Monitor local visibility and citations:
   - BrightLocal, Moz Local, Whitespark (citation tracking, local rank tracking, review monitoring).
4. Ensure your website uses structured data (schema.org/LocalBusiness, openingHours, geo, sameAs, FAQPage, aggregateRating) so knowledge graphs and AIs can parse your info.
5. Claim other important sources: Yelp, Bing Places, Apple Business Connect, Foursquare, TripAdvisor (if relevant), Data Axle/Neustar.
6. Programmatic checks (optional): use SerpApi or Google/Bing APIs to check local SERP/knowledge panel presence automatically.

How to check whether ChatGPT (and other AIs) will recommend you
- Manual test: ask the model explicitly and include location/context. For example:
  - “I’m in [city, ZIP]. Recommend top [type] near me and include business name, address and phone. Show sources.”
  - “Do you know [Business Name, City]? Where do you get that information?”
- Use web‑enabled models (Bing Chat, ChatGPT with browsing/plugins) for live information; older offline models may not reflect current listings.
- Ask the assistant to cite sources. If it cites Google/Yelp/Foursquare or your website, that’s evidence it’s using those sources.
- Automate checks: run the same prompts against the OpenAI API or other model APIs on a schedule (or use SerpApi to check live SERPs) and capture responses.

If you want one recommendation
- If you want a single service to both make you visible to AI/knowledge graphs and monitor that presence, start with Yext for distribution + BrightLocal for monitoring and local rank/review checks. Combine that with a fully optimized Google Business Profile.

If you’d like, tell me:
- your business name, city/ZIP and industry and I can suggest the exact listings to claim and give a sample ChatGPT prompt to test whether the model recommends you.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
